title: Knowledge Doc
content: PLEXUS FEATURES. Original 9 were cut to 6, framed as three jobs: Win the deal (RFP), Run the work (ActionSwarm, IT access, search), Control the spend (expenses, Zombie SaaS). F1 RFP and Security Questionnaire Engine (the wedge, real build): upload Excel/CSV, knowledge base of SOC2 docs/policies, answer per question with citation, confidence gate (auto-fill above threshold, red flag below with closest source), human review UI, learning loop (corrected answers saved and reused on next questionnaire), export .xlsx plus accuracy report. F2 ActionSwarm (real): meeting transcript to schema-forced JSON of action items, assignees, due dates; tasks on own dashboard board (real Jira optional); Slack summary post; email draft; live activity feed; injection guard that treats planted instructions as data. F3 OmniContext + Catch-Me-Up (Cmd+K, real over ~10 seeded docs): hybrid search with cited answers, permission-aware retrieval (intern vs founder salary-sheet demo; needs confirmation that Meko datapack sharing supports this), Catch-Me-Up is a time-window mode ("last 4 days") giving an executive briefing. F4 ZeroTouch Expenses (thin): 3-5 prepared receipts via Gemini vision, extract merchant/items/GST/total, policy check, one violation, card-feed matching. F5 Zero-Friction IT Provisioning (real logic): natural-language request ("I need Figma"), risk classification, role check, low-risk auto-grant, high-risk (AWS prod) manager Approve/Reject (dashboard button, Slack button if time), audit log and undo. F6 Zombie SaaS Eradicator (mocked on purpose): seeded billing and SSO login tables, one SQL join for tools paid for with zero logins in 30+ days, waste dashboard in rupees. CUT (roadmap slide only): Dynamic Pitch-Deck Compiler, Procurement and Contract Routing. Priority: RFP engine plus trust layer must never be cut; cut order if behind: Zombie SaaS, Expenses, Slack buttons, Catch-Me-Up. On slides use feature names, not numbers.

content:
Building with Al without losing hours

Test the riskiest piece (Meko) in the first two hours, then build one complete module per prompt, and commit after every working step.

1. Walking skeleton first. One button sends a request to Gemini, writes a memory and a trace to Meko, and shows both in the activity feed. If Meko is not working by 1:30 PM Saturday, switch to the fallback (own tables) and keep going.

One module per prompt. Each prompt states the goal, inputs, output schema, the files to touch and a test you can run. Paste the same short context file every time: stack, folder layout, environment variable names.

2.

3. Patches, not rewrites. Ask for changes to named files only, and paste the exact error plus the file when something breaks.

4. Batch model calls. Send RFP questions in groups of about 10 per call and add retry with backoff, so the Gemini free tier does not throttle your live demo.
